title: A codex seat plans and delivers over the real MCP wire
description:
SPIDR child 2 of task-969575299465484d9486ea02ff7ae336 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 task-8e793ae3c63f41189bcc05f6d7c15605, which makes the provider selectable.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: Codex MISSION PARITY and the offline proof. The mission text, the MCP result-size handling (the codex analogue of Claude's MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS, i.e. paged reads), the tool roster, and the work_get_context / work_release path must all work for a codex seat as they do for a claude one. No UI, no live drive - child 3.

THE WIRING ALREADY EXISTS, so this row is parity work, not integration from scratch. Measured at HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04): `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts:64-83,116-150` invokes `codex exec` with the mission ON STDIN via `-`, passes the scoped MCP bearer through an env var codex reads by name (`bearer_token_env_var`, :35) - never argv, never a file - and sets `--ignore-user-config` so the HOST's codex config cannot leak in. Config values are deliberately QUOTE-FREE because codex parses each `-c` value itself (:73). `agent-spawn-environment.ts:22-24` holds the CLOSED codex env allowlist, measured against codex-cli 0.147.0. README's own words are the gap: 'a Codex seat is wired but was last proven only to reach the API'.

THE PROOF IS A SCRIPTED DOUBLE, NOT THE REAL CLI. The parent's DoD 2 asks for a scripted `codex` double over the REAL MCP wire completing the planning reads plus `planning.submit_decomposition`, and a node.deliver reaching verifier ACCEPTED and lander COMMITTED. That is reachable offline and does not depend on the Codex quota (exhausted until 2026-09-08 when the parent was filed). The REAL `codex exec` run is child 3's live drive, and is explicitly allowed to report blocked on quota.

RESULT-SIZE HANDLING IS THE LIKELY REAL DEFECT. A seat that cannot page a large read silently truncates its context and plans against a partial contract. Claude's path uses paged reads because of MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS; measure what codex does with an oversized MCP result BEFORE assuming parity, and record the measurement.
definitionOfDone: A scripted `codex` double drives the REAL MCP wire end to end offline against a real daemon: the planning reads, then `planning.submit_decomposition` accepted; then a `node.deliver` reaching verifier ACCEPTED and lander COMMITTED. Assert the durable outcomes from the store (the sealed run, the verifier receipt, the landing sha), not the double's own exit code. `pnpm test:e2e` count line quoted with the new test named.

MCP RESULT-SIZE HANDLING MEASURED, not assumed: drive an oversized read through the codex path and record what happens. If codex truncates where claude pages, that is the defect this row fixes; if it does not, record the measurement that shows so. A seat that silently truncates its context plans against a partial contract and the failure appears later as a bad plan, not as an error.

The work_get_context / work_release path completes for a codex seat: the double claims, reads its own item, and RELEASES on the first try - reusing the observed-version disclosure task-f99cec0b landed (bootstrap-conflict-error.ts). Assert the release decision is EFFECTS_COMMITTED, not merely that the call returned.

The tool roster a codex seat sees equals the roster a claude seat sees for the same step kind - assert set-equality in both directions, because a missing tool makes a seat fail in a way that reads as a model problem rather than a wiring one.

The mission text a codex seat receives is asserted (it arrives on stdin via `-`, agent-spawner.ts:66-70): a produced codex mission contains the same load-bearing sentences as the claude one for the same step.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e`.
taskRails: OFFLINE PROOF ONLY. The real `codex exec` run is child 3's live drive; the Codex quota was exhausted until 2026-09-08 and this row must not depend on it.
THE DOUBLE GOES THROUGH THE REAL MCP WIRE with a scoped bearer and NEVER writes to the store directly - otherwise the journey proves the fixture, not the product.

NEVER WEAKEN THE CODEX SPAWN SURFACE to make a test pass: `--ignore-user-config`, the bearer-through-env-var-name (never argv, never a file), the closed CODEX_/OPENAI_ env allowlist and the quote-free `-c` values are all deliberate and measured against a specific codex-cli version. If one blocks the test, report it rather than relaxing it.
MEASURE RESULT-SIZE BEHAVIOUR before claiming parity. 'It worked on a small read' is not parity.
FEATURES ONLY (inherited): no security-boundary or policy work.

implementationPlan.description:

This row is a SPIDR shell: every criterion below was delegated to grandchild A (task-48932becda314704aad652b49a8d2209, roster + result-size + mission assertion) and grandchild B (task-ae309e473da84ef5ba43c11fdae96188, the scripted-double journey), both named in this row's dependsOn. Write NO new production code here — if a criterion is unmet, the fix belongs in the child that owns it, via a comment and an amendment on that row, not in a new diff here.

Read both children's `verification`, `completionSummary` and `reviewSummary` from get_context.epicSiblings rather than re-deriving their work. Then re-measure the two gaps this row was filed against, at the DELIVERED tree:
  (a) TOOL ROSTER — `grep -n 'allowedTools\|--tools\|CHAIN_TOOLS\|CODING_TOOLS' apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts apps/daemon/src/work/launch-template-producer.ts`. At plan time (2026-09-05) the codex argv at agent-spawner.ts:85-95 carried NO roster flags at all, only `--sandbox`; confirm a codex seat now gets a roster and that grandchild A's bidirectional set-equality arm exists and is not a subset check.
  (b) RESULT SIZE — `grep -n 'MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS' apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-environment.ts`. At plan time :71 set it unconditionally for every seat while its own comment named it as Claude's variable, so a codex seat had no result-size control. Confirm grandchild A RECORDED a measurement of codex's actual behaviour (command plus observed output, in its completionSummary or a row comment) rather than asserting parity — an unrecorded parity claim is the precise defect this row exists to prevent, and it is a reason to send the row back, not to re-measure it here.

Record what you found. If either child narrowed its DoD rather than closing its gap, say so plainly and route it back.

CONFIRM THE JOURNEY PROVES CODEX, NOT CLAUDE. Grandchild B's journey is only evidence if the codex branch actually ran. Two things to check at the delivered tree, both of which a green suite can hide:

  (a) THE SHIM NAME. The codex path is selected by the basename regex at apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts (`/(?:^|[\\/])codex(?:\.[a-z]+)?$/iu`). A shim named the existing harness way — `agent-codex.cmd`, from j1-loop-harness.ts:320 writeAgentShim — does NOT match it, because the character before "codex" is a hyphen rather than a path separator or the start of the string. Such a shim silently runs the CLAUDE branch and the journey goes green while proving nothing. Confirm the journey's shim matches the regex AND that an arm asserts the codex branch ran from something other than the filename (the codex-shaped argv, or the bearer-in-env path).
  (b) THE VERDICTS COME FROM THE STORE. Confirm ACCEPTED, COMMITTED and the EFFECTS_COMMITTED release are read off the durable ledger after the processes are dead — the j1-ledger-view.ts shape — and not from the double's exit code or stdout. Confirm the negative arm exists: a double that exits 0 without landing must FAIL the journey.

Also confirm grandchild B resolved constraint (3) from its description: `planning.submit_decomposition` is in the `withheld` set at apps/daemon/src/daemon-v2-command-registry.ts:211, so the journey either dispatches through a daemon without the v2 marker or asserts the exact roster refusal. A journey that quietly dropped that call satisfies no criterion.

GATES AND CLOSE. Run each leg STANDALONE and in the FOREGROUND — no pipe, no `;` chain, no `&&` (a piped run reports tail's exit code; a chain reports only the last command's):
  1. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`
  2. `pnpm typecheck`
  3. `pnpm test:e2e`

READ THE OUTPUT, NOT THE EXIT CODE. `pnpm --filter <pkg> <script>` prints "No projects matched the filters" and exits 0 when the filter misses; "No test files found" and "0 passed" are also exit 0. The discriminator is the `Test Files N passed` count line, which a vacuous run never prints — quote it for all three legs with N nonzero, and name grandchild B's new e2e test in the `pnpm test:e2e` output. Note that `pnpm test:e2e` runs `tsc -p tests/e2e/foundation/tsconfig.json` FIRST, so a harness type error fails the leg before any test runs; a tsc failure is not a test result. A bare `pnpm test` is not admissible for any apps/** claim here — the root vitest include has no `apps/**`.

Name `pnpm test:e2e` as this row's complete_task verification command. If a repo-wide leg is red, attribute it before treating it as yours: failures at the merge-base, failures at HEAD, subtract, intersect with this row's owned paths. This row owns NO production paths, so any red here belongs to a child or to a peer — report it verbatim with its exact failing lines and file paths, disclosed, never hidden and never fabricated green.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
SPLIT VS PLAN DIRECTLY. Planning this row as one task was rejected on measurement, not on feel: agent-spawner.ts, agent-spawn-environment.ts, launch-template-producer.ts, agent-mission-text.ts, their test files, a new codex double, a new e2e test and harness edits is >10 distinct files, which submit_plan hard-rejects, and the step list ran past 12.

WHERE THE SEAM WENT. SPIDR-Interface was the cut: grandchild A owns the SPAWN SURFACE (roster, result size, mission assertion) and is unit-tested in @moe/daemon; grandchild B owns the JOURNEY (the codex double and the e2e). That is also a contract boundary — B consumes the parity A lands — so the dependency is real build order, not paperwork. A three-way split that gave mission parity its own row was rejected once the mission surface measured provider-agnostic: that row would have been an assertion with no production work, i.e. an evidence row, which global rail 21 forbids.

WHY GRANDCHILD A KEEPS "AND" IN ITS TITLE. create_task warned on it. Roster and result size are separable in principle but land in the SAME two files (agent-spawner.ts, agent-spawn-environment.ts); splitting them would create two rows contending for one file, which the breakdown skill calls a sequencing decision rather than a split. Both halves are small. Kept together deliberately.

WHY THIS ROW'S dependsOn CHANGED. It previously named task-8e793ae3 (child 1, provider selectable). That was replaced by the two children. The offline proof does NOT need the durable provider setting: the codex branch is selected by the SHIM'S NAME, not by the stored provider, so gating the journey on 8e793ae3 and its five unlanded grandchildren would have cost real time for no safety. The genuine file-level ordering is carried instead by grandchild A's dependsOn on task-3a0478f5, the other row editing agent-spawner.ts.

WHAT THIS ROW BECOMES. A shell that composes and verifies. Its plan writes no production code; every criterion is delegated and a shortfall routes back to the owning child rather than being patched here.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED 2026-09-05 at branch moe/work-2026-09-04. This row was SPLIT rather than planned directly: the six DoD items spanned four production seams plus a new e2e journey, which measured past the plan caps (>10 distinct files, >12 steps). Two grandchildren were filed and this row's dependsOn was set to name both (it previously named task-8e793ae3; see the ordering note below).

GAP 1, TOOL ROSTER — the parent's DoD 4 was FALSE at plan time. `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts:85-95` composes the codex argv as exec/--ignore-user-config/--skip-git-repo-check/--ephemeral/--sandbox/-c url/-c bearer_token_env_var/- and carries NO tool roster flags at all. The claude argv at :107-109 passes `--tools CODING_BUILTIN_TOOLS` and `--allowedTools CODING_TOOLS|CHAIN_TOOLS` (constants at agent-spawn-environment.ts:10-12). Separately `apps/daemon/src/work/launch-template-producer.ts:106-107` composeArgv is hard claude-shaped (`["-p", "--allowedTools", ...]`, CLAUDE_LAUNCH_SELECTION_FLAGS, ClaudeLaunchSelection) with no codex branch, and is pinned by foundation-context-prelaunch.test.ts:274.

GAP 2, RESULT SIZE — `agent-spawn-environment.ts:71` sets MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS unconditionally for EVERY seat, and the comment above it names it as Claude's variable ("Claude's default (25000 tokens) spills a PRD-sized answer to disk", measured 2026-09-03 on UnAI's ~121 KB PRD). Codex does not read it, so a codex seat has NO result-size control. The description predicted this as "the likely real defect" and the measurement confirms it.

ALREADY CLOSED — the parent's DoD 5 (mission parity) is TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION and needs no production work. `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-mission-text.ts` exports codeMission/compilerMission/mission with no provider parameter and no codex branch (grep for "codex|provider" returns nothing), consumed only by agent-wrapper.ts:13. This is global rail 6's "gap claimed present, actually closed" direction: grandchild A asserts it rather than rebuilding it.

THE DOUBLE ALREADY EXISTS IN CLAUDE SHAPE — `tests/e2e/foundation/fake-agent.mjs` (315 lines) is a REAL-wire double: it opens an MCP session over HTTP with the scoped bearer, issues real JSON-RPC tools/call frames for work_get_context / review_submit / work_release, and never writes the store. `j1-loop-harness.ts:320` writeAgentShim emits the shim and passes it as MOE_AGENT_COMMAND at :360; `j1-ledger-view.ts` reads verdicts off the durable ledger after the processes die. So grandchild B copies a shape rather than inventing one.

THE SHIM-NAME TRAP — the codex branch is selected by the basename regex `/(?:^|[\\/])codex(?:\.[a-z]+)?$/iu` (agent-spawner.ts:~80). writeAgentShim currently emits `agent-<arm>.cmd`, and `agent-codex.cmd` does NOT match: the character before "codex" is a hyphen, not a separator or string start. A journey using the existing naming would run the CLAUDE branch and go green while proving nothing about codex. This is the single highest-value fact in the split.

CREDENTIAL PATH INVERTS — a claude seat gets a JSON file at `--mcp-config` (written at agent-spawner.ts:~119, only for non-codex seats); a codex seat gets neither. Its bearer arrives in the child's own env as MOE_AGENT_MCP_BEARER (CODEX_BEARER_VARIABLE at :37, injected at :156 AFTER the agentEnvironment spread, pinned by agent-spawner.test.ts:291) and its origin as the argv pair `-c mcp_servers.moe-next.url=<origin>`. fake-agent.mjs deliberately treats argv flags as non-evidence and reads everything from the config file; the codex double must do the exact inverse.
